claim: The Château de Crussol and its Ridges loop is a moderate ~4.8 km hike with ~210 m elevation gain, taking roughly 1.5–2 hours.
quote: moderate hike covering 3 miles with an elevation gain of 685 feet, taking about 1.5–2 hours to complete

claim: From the castle car park it is a 20-minute walk to the summit; from the Rhône Crussol Tourist Office, 40 minutes; a 3-hour circuit goes around the entire massif, with sturdy shoes recommended on rocky terrain.
quote: 20-minute walk to the summit from the castle car park; 40-minute walk starting from the Rhône Crussol Tourist Office; a 3-hour circuit trail labeled 'Crussol: a mountain packed with history'

claim: Crussol is exposed and arduous in hot weather — best months are April–June and September–October, water and sun protection essential, with only patchy forest shade.
quote: The climb can be arduous, especially in hot weather, and it's advisable to bring water and a hat to protect yourself from the sun. While the best time to visit is during spring and early autumn months from April to June and September to October

claim: Carbone Zéro at 24 rue Denis Papin, beside Valence's train station, rents both classic and electric bikes and is Accueil Vélo certified — the most convenient ViaRhôna rental in central Valence.
quote: Carbone Zéro - Magasin Cycles La Gare, 24 rue Denis Papin, 26000 Valence... a wide range of electric and classic bicycles along with rental services

claim: Around 130 e-bikes are spread across 35 ViaRhôna partners; daily rental sits at €35–55 and high-season reservation is recommended a month ahead.
quote: 130 electric bikes are distributed among 35 partners along ViaRhôna... daily rates of 35-55 € for quality electric bikes... advisable to reserve your electric bike at least a month in advance during high season

claim: The Tain-l'Hermitage to Valence ViaRhôna stretch is around 19 km of mostly asphalt greenway on stabilized track, an easy half-day ride through Hermitage vineyards and Rhône recreation areas.
quote: signposted linking route on stabilized greenway from Tain-l'Hermitage to La Roche-de-Glun bridge... asphalt greenway between La Roche-de-Glun and the entrance to Valence

claim: Bois des Naix offers a 5 km footpath across 12 hectares of mature trees with a fitness trail, playground, and the Vallée des Fleurs aquatic garden — easy family walking right in the agglomeration.
quote: Bois des Naix (in Valence) — Distance: 5km footpath. Features: '12-hectare green space' with mature trees, Vallée des Fleurs, aquatic plants, fitness trail, and children's playground

claim: Parc Jouvet is a 7-hectare riverside botanical garden classed as a 'Remarkable Garden' since 2006, sitting on the Rhône beneath the Champ de Mars with 700+ trees, canals, and rose gardens — the obvious river-walk start in town.
quote: Parc Jouvet is a 7-hectare public botanical garden located in Valence on the banks of the Rhône River, below the Champ de Mars esplanade... since 2006, Jouvet Park has been designated a 'Remarkable Garden'

claim: Col de Rousset (1,254 m tunnel) has two orientation tables giving 360° views of the climatic boundary between the green Northern Alps and Provence — a panoramic chair lift runs in summer to reach the upper belvedere without hiking.
quote: Two orientation tables allow you to discover a magnificent panorama: one located at the exit of the tunnel on the Diois side, the other at the top of the resort chairlift (accessible in summer and winter by chairlift...)

claim: Col de Tourniol (1,145 m), reached via Barbières, is one of the western entry gates to the Vercors with a quiet road and beautiful viewpoints — under an hour from Valence and a good easy Vercors-edge driving option.
quote: The Col de Tourniol at 1,145m is one of the entry gates to the western side of the Vercors massif, featuring a quiet road with beautiful viewpoints and pleasant, moderately challenging grades

claim: Col de la Bataille (1,313 m) above Léoncel offers a fabulous panorama of the Vercors combes and cliffs and is one of the rare road passes into the south Vercors, around 45 minutes from Valence.
quote: The Col de la Bataille at 1,313 meters altitude is one of the rare road passages allowing access to the South-Vercors... The panorama of the combes and cliffs is fabulous!

claim: Bois des Naix is described as the second-largest urban park in the former Rhône-Alpes region, maintained chemical-free, with 140 animal species and a permanent orienteering course of 20 beacons — bikes, music, and dogs are prohibited.
quote: Bois des Naix is the 2nd largest urban park in the Rhône-Alpes region... 140 animal species, some considered 'remarkable'... permanent orienteering course where you can search for 20 beacons... Bicycles, music, and animals are prohibited
